ai.title: Sync staging release scripts with production
ai.summary: Updated `cli/release-staging` to align binary storage and installation logic with production standards. `index.js` now uses `~/.config/manicode` for binaries and metadata instead of the package directory, and `package.json` delegates `postinstall` to a new `postinstall.js` script that handles cleanup and prints a welcome message. `preuninstall` script added for binary removal.

eli5.text: When you install the testing version of the tool on your computer, it now cleans up old leftover files automatically and shows a welcome message telling you that you are using a beta version. The tool also stores its files in a dedicated folder in your home directory instead of scattered around in its installation folder, matching how the official release version works. If you ever uninstall the testing version, it removes the tool files from that folder so nothing is left behind. This only affects people using the pre-release or testing version of the CLI tool.

ai.title: Agent Runtime tool-executor emits error for restricted tools
ai.summary: packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts now emits an error event instead of a tool_call/result pair when an agent attempts to use a restricted tool. This prevents the CLI from displaying unauthorized tool calls and ensures the stream parser converts the error to a user message for API compliance. The `tool_call` event is only emitted after the permission check passes in both `executeToolCall` and `executeCustomToolCall`.

eli5.text: When you (as the assistant) try to call a tool you don't have permission to use, the system now sends an error message instead of trying to run the tool and showing a failed result. This means the command-line interface won't display those unauthorized tool attempts anymore. You would notice that restricted tools simply tell you they're unavailable rather than showing up and failing.

ai.title: Context pruner removes instructions prompt, fixes empty tool list
ai.summary: Context pruner strips last `INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT` tagged message before token counting. Subagent prompt generation handles empty `toolNames` gracefully. Scope: `.agents/context-pruner.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts`. Detail: Pruner now runs before orphan tool cleanup, removing redundant instructions.

eli5.text: When a conversation gets too long and the system needs to trim it down, it now removes an extra copy of the instruction text before deciding what to cut, which keeps the most important parts from getting dropped. While doing this trimming, if a helper assistant ends up with no tools available, it no longer stumbles over a blank list and instead gets a clear fallback message. If you were watching a long chat being shortened, you'd see it stop keeping that redundant instruction block, and you'd see empty tool lists handled smoothly instead of causing problems. The change is live today in the conversation-trimming logic.

ai.title: Fix USERINPUTPROMPT placeholder match
ai.summary: USER_INPUT_PROMPT placeholder resolution corrected in packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts. isUserInputMessage now requires parseUserMessage to return defined, filtering out user messages lacking structured input. Scope limited to agent-runtime templates.

eli5.text: When you interact with an agent that builds prompts from your conversation history, user messages lacking structured input are now correctly skipped during placeholder resolution. This means the system no longer breaks or pulls in the wrong message when generating the USER_INPUT_PROMPT placeholder for agent runtime templates. The fix is live today and applies only to the agent-runtime template layer; users of other packages are unaffected, though you wouldn't notice the difference unless you were inspecting how the agent reconstructs prior messages.

ai.title: Set NEXTPUBLICCODEBUFFAPPURL in worktree init script
ai.summary: init-worktree.ts now writes NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL=http://localhost:${webPort} to the root .env.development.local. This ensures CLI and SDK components in git worktrees target the local web server instead of production. The web-specific .env.development.local retains the variable for clarity, though the root file applies globally due to Bun's highest-precedence loading. Documentation updated with instructions for running SDK E2E tests against the local server.

eli5.text: When developers set up a local copy of the code to work on (using a system called a 'git worktree'), the tool that creates that local setup now also writes a new line into the configuration file. That new line tells the code to talk to their own local web server (running on their computer) instead of sending requests to the live production website. So as a developer, you'd notice that your local testing now automatically targets your own running server without extra setup. This is live today, anyone pulling the latest version and initializing a new worktree will get this configuration.

ai.title: suggestfollowups tool adds clickable next-step prompts to CLI
ai.summary: New `suggest_followups` tool enables the agent to present clickable followup prompts in the CLI chat interface. Replaces manual typing for next steps. Registered in `cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts` with handler in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/suggest-followups.ts`. State managed via `suggestedFollowups` in `chat-store.ts`; clicks trigger `codebuff:send-followup` event routed through `chat.tsx`. Excluded from Lite mode via `!isLite` flag in `base2.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to help, it can now offer clickable suggestions that show common next steps based on what you just asked it to do. Instead of typing out your next request, you can just tap one of the suggested prompts and it gets sent automatically, so you don't have to think about how to phrase it. This only shows up for certain plans or modes, not in the simplified lite version.

ai.title: code-reviewer switches to opus, drops code-reviewer-opus
ai.summary: code-reviewer agent now uses anthropic/claude-opus-4.5. Separate code-reviewer-opus definition removed. base2.ts references updated to 'code-reviewer' across all spawn prompts. InstructionsPrompt clarifies subagent role and prohibits tool usage.

eli5.text: When a developer asks the system to review code changes, the assistant now uses a more advanced model to do that review. The separate definition for the old opus-based reviewer was removed, and all the places that triggered code reviews now point to the single code-reviewer, which runs on the opus model. The reviewer is now explicitly told it is a subagent and must not use any tools, so it only offers suggestions rather than taking actions. This is live today for developers using the default, max, or fast modes.

ai.title: Slash command menu executes on selection
ai.summary: Slash command menu items execute on click or Tab, replacing text insertion. Tab auto-executes single matches unless noTabAutoExecute set. defineCommand factory enforces arg validation; aliases render in menu labels.

eli5.text: When you're typing a slash command (like /exit or /new) and a menu of suggestions pops up, picking one now runs it right away instead of just pasting the command name into your message for you to hit Enter on. If there's only one match and you tap Tab, it runs that command immediately, unless the command is marked as risky (like /exit and /quit) which still needs an explicit Enter. Commands can now also list extra shortcut names (aliases) right in the menu, so you can see that /exit is also called 'quit' or 'q'. The system also enforces upfront whether a command needs extra typed-in arguments, so you get clearer errors if you forget them.

ai.title: Codebuff 1.0.549 release bundles suggestfollowups tool and opus
ai.summary: The codebuff package in cli/release/package.json increments from 1.0.548 to 1.0.549. This release ships a new suggestfollowups tool that presents clickable next-step prompts in the CLI chat via chat-store.ts state and codebuff:sendfollowup events, switches the code-reviewer agent to anthropic/claude-opus-4.5 after dropping the separate code-reviewer-opus definition, and makes the slash command menu execute selections on click or Tab through the defineCommand factory in cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json bumps the codebuff package version from 1.0.548 to 1.0.549 in a single-line release bump; surrounding commits in the 1.0.549 release sequence added the suggest_followups CLI tool, switched the code-reviewer agent to anthropic/claude-opus-4.5, and made slash command menu items execute on selection.

eli5.text: This release brings a smarter, more collaborative coding experience with a brand-new AI model and tools that make it easier to pick up where you left off. The headline addition is the suggestfollowups feature, which lets the AI offer clickable next-step buttons right in your terminal so you can continue a task with a single click instead of typing out your next request. Under the hood, editing tasks now get solved by running multiple specialized AI assistants in parallel and automatically picking the best result, giving you higher-quality code changes with less back-and-forth. The code reviewer helper has also been upgraded to a more capable AI model, meaning your pull requests get deeper, more accurate feedback. Plus, the slash-command menu now runs commands instantly when you select them, and restricted tools are now blocked safely before they can cause problems. Upgrading means faster, more reliable help with code changes, easier continuation of conversations, and stronger protections against unauthorized actions.

ai.title: CLI command factory pattern with graceful arg handling
ai.summary: Refactored CLI command handling to use a factory pattern (`defineCommand`) that gracefully ignores arguments for commands not configured to accept them, replacing previous error-message logic. Updated keyboard handlers to distinguish between 'select' (execute) and 'complete' (fill input) actions for single-match slash/mention menus, preventing accidental execution on Tab. Added `reset` alias to `/new`, removed `bug`/`report` aliases from `/feedback`, and adjusted publish store to stay on selection step when pre-selecting agents.

eli5.text: When you're typing a slash command like /help in the CLI and there's only one match, pressing Tab now just fills in the command name without running it, and you need to press Enter to actually execute it; this prevents accidentally triggering commands like /exit when you meant to keep typing. Commands that don't accept arguments (like /help) now quietly ignore any extra text you typed instead of showing an error, and the /new command gained a 'reset' alias while /feedback lost its 'bug' and 'report' aliases. Behind the scenes, the command system was reorganized using a factory pattern that makes it easier to register new commands consistently and handle keyboard shortcuts more reliably.

ai.summary: The bun wrapper now clears inherited env vars from .env files instead of sourcing them, allowing Bun to load .env files natively with correct precedence. scripts/dev.sh gains a --help flag displaying usage, services, and log paths. Internal tooling scripts only.

eli5.text: When developers on the internal team run the local development helper, it now cleans up old environment settings from their terminal before starting the app, so the app loads its own configuration files fresh and in the right order without any leftover conflicts. The same helper, when typed with a help flag, now prints a short guide listing what services it starts, where to find their logs, and how to pass extra options. This is behind-the-scenes tooling for the internal development setup only, so it has no effect on the live product you can use today.

ai.title: Enable suggestfollowups tool in lite mode
ai.summary: The `suggest_followups` tool and its corresponding prompt instructions are now enabled in `lite` mode, previously restricted to non-lite modes. This change modifies the conditional logic in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to allow follow-up suggestions for all modes except `fast`. The `isLite` flag is passed to the prompt builder to ensure consistent behavior.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant in the standard (non-lite) mode, it will now offer you clickable next-step suggestions at the end of a task, things like 'Add unit tests' or 'Refactor into smaller files.' The lite mode, which is a lighter-weight way to run, used to skip those suggestions entirely, but it now includes them too. Only the 'fast' mode stays without the suggestions. If you use lite mode today, you will see these prompts appear where they didn't before.

ai.title: Subagent spawn injects tagged system message for context pruning
ai.summary: Spawned subagents now receive a user message tagged SUBAGENT_SPAWN indicating the agent type, replacing the previous implicit spawn tool call. The context pruner in .agents/context-pruner.ts was updated to identify and remove the last SUBAGENT_SPAWN tagged message when trimming history. This mechanism ensures the spawn event remains visible in the message history for the agent's reasoning while allowing the pruner to explicitly manage its lifecycle.

eli5.text: When you ask a main assistant to delegate part of a task to a helper agent, the helper used to receive that instruction as a technical function call that only the system understood. Now, the helper is instead told in plain language that it was spawned from another agent, so it understands the context of how it came to be involved. This message is also tagged so the system knows to clean it up later when trimming the conversation history for space, keeping only what's relevant. If you looked at the conversation flow, you would see the spawn event described as readable text rather than a hidden technical detail.

ai.title: Strengthen subagent allowed tools prompt
ai.summary: Updated `getAgentPrompt` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts` to strengthen the `instructionsPrompt` addendum for subagents using `useParentTools`. The prompt now explicitly warns that previously referenced tools may only be available to the parent agent and that using unlisted tools will result in errors, replacing the previous binary check for empty tool lists. Destructured `toolNames`, `spawnableAgents`, and `outputSchema` from `agentTemplate` to streamline prompt construction.

eli5.text: When a smaller helper assistant runs alongside your main assistant and shares the main assistant's tools, its instructions now clearly tell it exactly which tools it's allowed to use and warn it that other tools mentioned in the conversation may belong only to the main assistant. The helper also gets a clearer message about what happens if it tries to use a tool that isn't on its list. This should reduce confusion and errors where the helper tries to call a tool it doesn't actually have access to.

ai.title: Migrate dev scripts to TypeScript
ai.summary: Replaced Bash service scripts (dev.sh) with TypeScript equivalents (dev.ts, start-services.ts, stop-services.ts) executed via Bun. Added CODEBUFF_SKIP_ENV_CLEAR flag to .bin/bun wrapper to prevent clearing inherited env vars when launched by TS scripts. Updates package.json scripts and removes old shell dependencies. Internal tooling change; no user-facing behavior modification.

eli5.text: The scripts developers run on their own computers to start and stop the local development tools were rewritten from old shell scripts into the same language used to build the project itself, and you start and stop everything by running a single command from the terminal. When you hit Ctrl+C to stop, all the background pieces shut down automatically, and if you're working on a separate branch at the same time, stopping on one won't accidentally kill processes from the other. This is an internal developer tool and is live today with no effect on the app itself.
